```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(here)
library(tidyverse)
here::i_am("errata.qmd")

out <- function(f) read_csv(here("maintained", "output", f), show_col_types = FALSE)

advantage <- out("text_observational_experience_advantage.csv")
dataset <- out("text_observational_dataset_description.csv")

figure_3_np <- out("figure_3_mturk_main_candidate_pref.csv") |>
  filter(panel == "Nonpartisan", !is.na(estimate))
pol_np <- filter(figure_3_np, coef_group == "Pol. Experience")
largest_other <- max(abs(figure_3_np$estimate[figure_3_np$coef_group != "Pol. Experience"]))

# Race preferences by respondent party, both samples, both ballot types.
race <- bind_rows(
  mutate(out("figure_5_mturk_het_fx_candidate_pref.csv"), sample = "Mechanical Turk"),
  mutate(out("figure_6_yougov_het_fx_candidate_pref.csv"), sample = "YouGov")
) |>
  filter(panel %in% c("Nonpartisan", "Partisan"), coef_group == "Race", !is.na(estimate))

race_pp <- function(sample_label, party_label, level, panel_label = "Nonpartisan") {
  100 * race$estimate[race$sample == sample_label & race$party == party_label &
                        race$label == level & race$panel == panel_label]
}

race_list <- function(sample_label, party_label, panel_label = "Nonpartisan") {
  rows <- filter(race, sample == sample_label, party == party_label, panel == panel_label)
  paste0(rows$label, " ", sprintf("%+.1f", 100 * rows$estimate), collapse = ", ")
}

# The difference column of Figure 7: political experience on competence ratings.
competence_diff <- out("figure_7_mturk_het_fx_competence.csv") |>
  filter(panel == "Difference", coef_group == "Pol. Experience", !is.na(estimate)) |>
  mutate(clears_zero = conf.low > 0 | conf.high < 0)

clears <- function(party_label) {
  sum(competence_diff$clears_zero[competence_diff$party == party_label])
}

n_per_party <- sum(competence_diff$party == "Democrats")
republican_mayor <- filter(competence_diff, party == "Republicans", label == "Mayor")

# What entry 3's cell is read against: Figure 8's difference column, and the vote-choice
# difference for the same Republican cell in Figure 5.
competence_diff_yougov <- out("figure_8_yougov_het_fx_competence.csv") |>
  filter(panel == "Difference", coef_group == "Pol. Experience", !is.na(estimate)) |>
  mutate(clears_zero = conf.low > 0 | conf.high < 0)

clears_yougov <- function(party_label) {
  sum(competence_diff_yougov$clears_zero[competence_diff_yougov$party == party_label])
}

n_per_party_yougov <- sum(competence_diff_yougov$party == "Democrats")
n_republican_cells <- n_per_party + n_per_party_yougov
republican_mayor_vote <- out("figure_5_mturk_het_fx_candidate_pref.csv") |>
  filter(panel == "Difference", coef_group == "Pol. Experience", party == "Republicans",
         label == "Mayor")

pol_np_sorted <- arrange(pol_np, desc(estimate))

# The prose below spells small counts out, so the counts derived from the spine are
# spelled out too rather than printed as digits.
spelled <- function(n) {
  words <- c("one", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six", "seven", "eight", "nine", "ten")
  if_else(n >= 1 & n <= 10, words[n], as.character(n))
}
```

```{r entries}
# THE ERRATA SPINE. Every entry is defined once, here, and the document below is rendered
# from it. The same rows are written out as errata_entries.csv at the foot of this file, so
# anything else that needs the corrections (the README's count, a remastered edition) reads
# them rather than keeping a hand-typed copy that can drift out of agreement with this one.
#
# Every corrected value is computed at render time from maintained/output/. A number is
# never typed into a corrected field: str_glue() keeps the pipeline in the loop, which is
# the whole reason this note cannot go stale in the way the article did.
#
# [[...]] marks the span that changes, and is the only markup in the published and corrected
# fields. Each renderer resolves it its own way: bold here, a macro in a later edition. Entry 2
# carries no marker in its published field: the correction there is a pure insertion of two
# qualifying clauses, so no span of the published sentence is wrong to mark.
#
# `location` is where the sentence sits in the published article, taken verbatim from this
# repo's own extraction, ground_truth/published_claims.csv, prefixed with "published " to match
# the convention used across these notes. This document does not print it; it is carried for
# the consumers that read errata_entries.csv, which is also why it must stay a character
# column rather than an empty one that read_csv types as logical.
#
# Numbering is the published note's and is APPEND-ONLY: an entry can already have been cited
# by number, so a later finding is added at the end and never interleaved, renumbered,
# merged or split.
#
# `claim_ids` names the ground truth rows the entry corrects, semicolon separated, and it is
# what makes "has this finding been published?" a query over the corpus rather than a reading
# of every note. It is empty where the entry has no ground truth row: a reference list is not
# an extraction claim. Every id listed here is checked against the ground truth by
# ground_truth/build_ground_truth.R, which refuses to finish on a dangling one.
entries <- tribble(
  ~entry, ~class, ~source, ~form, ~title, ~location, ~published, ~corrected, ~note, ~claim_ids,

  1, "label", "pipeline", "full",
  "The two ballot types are transposed in the experience-advantage comparison",
  "published Observational evidence, p. 6",
  "Subsetting our dataset to only those elections in which candidates have different levels of political experience (779 elections), we see that the candidate with more experience wins about [[62%]] of the time in [[partisan]] elections and [[61%]] of the time in [[nonpartisan]] elections.",
  str_glue("Subsetting our dataset to only those elections in which candidates have different levels of political experience (779 elections), we see that the candidate with more experience wins about [[{sprintf('%.0f', advantage$pct_nonpartisan)}%]] of the time in [[nonpartisan]] elections and [[{sprintf('%.0f', advantage$pct_partisan)}%]] of the time in [[partisan]] elections."),
  str_glue(
    "Both percentages are right and the labels attached to them are the wrong way round. ",
    "The data give {sprintf('%.1f', advantage$pct_nonpartisan)} per cent in nonpartisan ",
    "elections and {sprintf('%.1f', advantage$pct_partisan)} per cent in partisan ",
    "elections, across the {advantage$n_elections_total} elections the sentence identifies. ",
    "The direction matters here, because the article's own argument is that nonpartisan ",
    "ballots favour the more experienced candidate: the published sentence reports the gap ",
    "running the other way. What the sentence holds up is the paragraph's verdict that this ",
    "analysis \"paints a murkier picture\". Corrected, the gap runs the way the paper ",
    "predicts, by {sprintf('%.1f', advantage$difference_pp)} percentage points at ",
    "p = {sprintf('%.3f', advantage$p_value_hc2)} (entry 4), so the verdict survives on the ",
    "absence of a difference rather than on its sign. The observational support the ",
    "Discussion draws on is Table 1, which this entry does not touch."),
  "obs_partisan_more_experienced_wins_pct;obs_nonpartisan_more_experienced_wins_pct",

  2, "definition", "pipeline", "full",
  "The racial preference pattern holds in one sample and not the other",
  "published Results: Figures 5 and 6, p. 15",
  "Republican respondents marginally prefer white candidates while Democrats marginally prefer nonwhite candidates.",
  "Republican respondents marginally prefer white candidates [[in the YouGov sample]], while Democrats marginally prefer nonwhite [[candidates in both]].",
  str_glue(
    "The Democratic half of the sentence holds everywhere: all six estimates are positive, ",
    "{race_list('Mechanical Turk', 'Democrats')} percentage points on Mechanical Turk and ",
    "{race_list('YouGov', 'Democrats')} on YouGov, the last of those being ",
    "{sprintf('%+.3f', race_pp('YouGov', 'Democrats', 'Hispanic'))} rather than a true ",
    "zero. The Republican half holds only on YouGov, where the three estimates are ",
    "{race_list('YouGov', 'Republicans')}. On Mechanical Turk, Republican respondents ",
    "prefer **Asian** candidates to white candidates by ",
    "{sprintf('%.1f', race_pp('Mechanical Turk', 'Republicans', 'Asian'))} percentage ",
    "points, while preferring white candidates to Black ones by ",
    "{sprintf('%.1f', -race_pp('Mechanical Turk', 'Republicans', 'Black'))} and to Hispanic ",
    "ones by {sprintf('%.1f', -race_pp('Mechanical Turk', 'Republicans', 'Hispanic'))}. ",
    "A reader taking the sentence as a general finding about Republican respondents would ",
    "be taking a pattern that reverses on one of the paper's two samples. The qualification ",
    "applies under both ballots, which keeps the next sentence's \"these race and gender ",
    "patterns do not differ much by election type\" true: in partisan elections the ",
    "Republican estimates are {race_list('Mechanical Turk', 'Republicans', 'Partisan')} on ",
    "Mechanical Turk and {race_list('YouGov', 'Republicans', 'Partisan')} on YouGov. Nothing ",
    "later in the article rests on the race pattern, which it offers as one of \"some small ",
    "patterns\"; the abstract and the Discussion rest on political and career experience."),
  "desc_race_preference_by_respondent_party",

  3, "definition", "pipeline", "full",
  "Republican respondents do show a competence gap by election type",
  "published Mechanism: Figures 7 and 8, p. 17",
  "As shown in the difference column, Democratic respondents ([[but not Republican respondents]]) rate such candidates as even more competent in the absence of party labels.",
  "As shown in the difference column, Democratic respondents ([[and, for candidates who have been mayor, Republican respondents]]) rate such candidates as even more competent in the absence of party labels.",
  str_glue(
    "The parenthetical reads the Republican half of Figure 7's difference column as null, ",
    "and one of its four estimates is not. {clears('Democrats')} of the {n_per_party} ",
    "Democratic intervals exclude zero and so does {clears('Republicans')} of the ",
    "{n_per_party} Republican ones: Republican respondents rate a candidate who has been ",
    "mayor {sprintf('%.2f', republican_mayor$estimate)} points more competent in ",
    "nonpartisan than in partisan elections, with a 95 per cent interval of ",
    "{sprintf('%.2f', republican_mayor$conf.low)} to ",
    "{sprintf('%.2f', republican_mayor$conf.high)}. The contrast the sentence draws is one ",
    "of degree rather than of presence. What the parenthetical held up is the section's ",
    "parallel between the two outcomes: \"the same candidate types that respondents view as ",
    "more competent are the ones that they tend to elect at higher rates in nonpartisan ",
    "elections.\" For Democratic respondents the parallel holds. For the corrected ",
    "Republican cell it does not, since in Figure 5's difference column the same ",
    "respondents are {sprintf('%.1f', -100 * republican_mayor_vote$estimate)} percentage ",
    "points less likely to choose a former mayor in nonpartisan elections (95 per cent ",
    "interval {sprintf('%.1f', 100 * republican_mayor_vote$conf.low)} to ",
    "{sprintf('%.1f', 100 * republican_mayor_vote$conf.high)}). It is also one Republican ",
    "interval in {n_republican_cells}: Figure 8's YouGov difference column has ",
    "{clears_yougov('Republicans')} of {n_per_party_yougov} Republican intervals excluding ",
    "zero (and {clears_yougov('Democrats')} of {n_per_party_yougov} Democratic ones), and at ",
    "the 5 per cent level chance alone gives {sprintf('%.2f', 0.05 * n_republican_cells)} ",
    "such intervals in {n_republican_cells}. The competence argument survives, resting on ",
    "Democratic respondents, who are also the ones for whom the vote-choice results bear ",
    "out the paper's main prediction."),
  "desc_democrats_competence_gap_nonpartisan",

  4, "quantity", "pipeline", "full",
  "The p-value on the experience-advantage comparison reproduces under no test",
  "published Observational evidence, p. 6",
  "This difference is not statistically significant (p = [[0.791]]).",
  str_glue("This difference is not statistically significant (p = [[{sprintf('%.3f', advantage$p_value_hc2)}]])."),
  str_glue(
    "The corrected figure is a regression of the more-experienced-candidate-wins indicator ",
    "on ballot type with HC2 standard errors. A chi-squared test of the same two-by-two ",
    "table gives {sprintf('%.3f', advantage$p_value_chisq)}, and no standard test of this ",
    "comparison returns 0.791. The conclusion the sentence draws is unaffected: the ",
    "difference of {sprintf('%.1f', advantage$difference_pp)} percentage points is not ",
    "distinguishable from zero on any of them. No other sentence quotes the p-value, so ",
    "\"not statistically significant\" is the whole of what it holds up."),
  "obs_experience_advantage_p_value",

  5, "quantity", "pipeline", "full",
  "The number of municipalities in the mayoral election dataset",
  "published Information Shortcuts in Nonpartisan Elections, p. 6",
  "This dataset covers [[225]] unique municipalities and records background characteristics of winners and runners-up, contextual information such as electoral rules, and electoral outcomes.",
  str_glue("This dataset covers [[{dataset$n_municipalities}]] unique municipalities and records background characteristics of winners and runners-up, contextual information such as electoral rules, and electoral outcomes."),
  str_glue(
    "The file carries {dataset$n_municipalities} distinct FIPS place codes across its ",
    "{dataset$n_elections} elections, and it is the file the sentence describes: the ",
    "election count and the {dataset$year_first} to {dataset$year_last} span both reproduce ",
    "exactly. No other reading of it returns 225 either, since municipalities holding more ",
    "than one election number 171, the subset used later in the paragraph covers 216, and ",
    "truncating the place code to five digits gives 213. No quantity in the article is ",
    "computed over municipalities: Table 1 and the experience-advantage comparison count ",
    "elections, so the correction changes the description of the dataset and nothing ",
    "derived from it."),
  "obs_n_municipalities",

  6, "quantity", "pipeline", "full",
  "The range of political experience effects is stated more tightly than the estimates support",
  "published Results: Figure 3, p. 12",
  "Relative to a candidate with no political experience, respondents prefer candidates who are City Council Members, State Legislators, Mayors, or Representatives in Congress by a margin of [[25--30]] percentage points.",
  str_glue("Relative to a candidate with no political experience, respondents prefer candidates who are City Council Members, State Legislators, Mayors, or Representatives in Congress by a margin of [[{sprintf('%.0f', 100 * min(pol_np$estimate))}--{sprintf('%.0f', 100 * max(pol_np$estimate))}]] percentage points."),
  str_glue(
    "The published range is wrong at both ends rather than at one. The four estimates in ",
    "the nonpartisan column of Figure 3 are ",
    "{paste0(pol_np$label, ' ', sprintf('%.1f', 100 * pol_np$estimate), collapse = ', ')} ",
    "percentage points. The claim the sentence makes is unaffected: political experience ",
    "remains by a wide margin the most consequential attribute in the figure, and the next ",
    "largest effect of any kind is {sprintf('%.1f', 100 * largest_other)} percentage points. ",
    "The corrected upper end also bears on the sentence that follows, that candidates who ",
    "had been mayor \"were rewarded most\": {pol_np_sorted$label[1]}'s ",
    "{sprintf('%.1f', 100 * pol_np_sorted$estimate[1])} stands ",
    "{sprintf('%.1f', 100 * (pol_np_sorted$estimate[1] - pol_np_sorted$estimate[2]))} points ",
    "above the next largest, {pol_np_sorted$label[2]}'s ",
    "{sprintf('%.1f', 100 * pol_np_sorted$estimate[2])}, a lead the published range ",
    "understated."),
  "results_pol_exp_range_low;results_pol_exp_range_high",

  7, "bibliographic", "reference_audit", "brief",
  "Oliver, Ha and Callen (2012) is missing its third author",
  "published references, p. 590",
  "[[Oliver, J. E., & Ha, S. E.]] (2012). Local Elections and the Politics of Small-Scale Democracy. Princeton: Princeton University Press.",
  "Oliver, J. E., Ha, S. E., & Callen, Z. (2012). Local Elections and the Politics of Small-Scale Democracy. Princeton: Princeton University Press.",
  paste("The book has three authors. Crossref, doi 10.23943/princeton/9780691143552.001.0001:",
        "Oliver, J. Eric; Ha, Shang E.; Callen, Zachary. The article's own in-text citation on",
        "p. 588 reads \"Oliver et al. 2012\", which the two-author entry cannot support.",
        "No claim in the article rests on the author list; what the correction restores is",
        "the reference's function, that the citation leads a reader to the book it names."),
  ""
) |>
  mutate(across(c(title, published, corrected, note, claim_ids), as.character))

stopifnot(nrow(entries) == max(entries$entry), !anyDuplicated(entries$entry))

# The spine's markup, resolved for this document.
bold <- function(x) str_replace_all(x, "\\[\\[(.*?)\\]\\]", "**\\1**")
```

This note lists `r spelled(nrow(entries))` errors in "Candidate Choice Without Party Labels: New Insights from Conjoint Survey Experiments," published in *Political Behavior* 40(3), doi [10.1007/s11109-017-9414-8](https://doi.org/10.1007/s11109-017-9414-8). **None of them changes a conclusion of the article.** `r str_to_sentence(spelled(sum(entries$class %in% c("label", "quantity"))))` are misstated numbers, `r spelled(sum(entries$class == "definition"))` are descriptions of the figures that the estimates behind those figures do not support, and `r spelled(sum(entries$class == "bibliographic"))` is an author missing from a reference-list entry. Each is recorded because a reader who quoted the article would be quoting something the record does not bear out.

Every corrected value in entries 1 to `r max(entries$entry[entries$class != "bibliographic"])` is computed from the data at the time this document is rendered: the conjoint estimates from the deposited replication archive ([10.7910/DVN/WSUHI3](https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/WSUHI3)), and the mayoral election data from the file the authors supplied, which the deposit omits. The reference-list entry is verified against the authoritative record at Crossref, named in the entry. The code supporting each correction is at [github.com/active-maintenance-aec/kirkland_coppock_2018](https://github.com/active-maintenance-aec/kirkland_coppock_2018).

```{r emit-entries, results="asis"}
# A heading is only a heading when a blank line precedes it, so each entry opens with one.
walk(seq_len(nrow(entries)), function(i) {
  e <- entries[i, ]
  cat("\n\n## ", e$entry, ". ", e$title, "\n\n> ", bold(e$published), "\n\nCorrected:\n\n> ",
      bold(e$corrected), "\n\n", e$note, "\n", sep = "")
})
```

```{r emit-spine}
# The machine-readable spine, written wherever this document is rendered. Anything else that
# states these corrections or counts them reads this file rather than retyping them.
write_csv(entries, here("errata_entries.csv"))
```
